name: Zophar
title: Job's friend from Na'amah
summary: Zophar from Na'amah was one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him in his suffering. He is known for his sharp speeches in which he accused Job of hidden sin and urged him to repent. In the end, he was rebuked by God for not speaking rightly about Him, as Job had done.

keyEvents.title: Zophar comes to comfort Job
keyEvents.description: Zophar from Na'amah came together with Eliphaz and Bildad to show Job compassion and comfort him in his great suffering. They sat with him for seven days without saying a word.

keyEvents.title: Zophar's first speech – accusation of hidden sin
keyEvents.description: In his first speech, Zophar accused Job of speaking emptily and urged him to turn to God. He claimed that God was actually punishing Job less than his sins deserved.

keyEvents.title: Zophar describes the depth of God's wisdom
keyEvents.description: Zophar challenged Job by pointing out that God's wisdom is deeper than Sheol and broader than the sea, and that humans cannot fully grasp it.

keyEvents.title: Zophar's second speech – the fate of the wicked
keyEvents.description: In his second speech, Zophar described the short-lived happiness of the wicked and their inevitable downfall. He painted a dramatic picture of how the wealth and joy of the ungodly are only temporary.

keyEvents.title: Zophar urges Job to repent
keyEvents.description: Zophar urged Job to direct his heart toward God and stretch out his hands to Him, promising that this would lead to restoration and security.

keyEvents.title: God rebukes Zophar and his friends
keyEvents.description: God spoke to Eliphaz and included Zophar in His rebuke, saying they had not spoken rightly about Him as Job had. They were told to offer burnt offerings and have Job pray for them.
